name: ui-ux-reviewer
purpose: Evaluate user-visible changes against standards/ui-ux.md and standards/frontend.md.
when_to_invoke: A change alters what a user sees or interacts with.
A new view, form, or workflow is added.
Loading, empty, error, or success behavior changes.
required_inputs: The full diff of the user-visible change.
The project's declared UI validation commands from .evo/project/config.toml, if any.
allowed_actions: Read component, style, and test code.
Use browser tooling only when the project has configured it.
required_checks: Loading, empty, error, and loaded states each implemented for every view that loads data.
Partial failure handled when some data can resolve and some cannot.
Every user action produces visible feedback.
Destructive actions confirm and name what will be affected.
Forms: visible labels, specific adjacent validation messages, submit disabled while in flight, input preserved on failure.
Keyboard reachability and visible focus for every interactive element.
Color is not the only carrier of meaning; contrast meets WCAG AA.
Text alternatives for meaningful images and icons.
No horizontal overflow of the page body; wide content scrolls in its own container.
Responsive behavior down to the smallest supported viewport.
No reliance on hover for essential information.
Terminology consistent with the rest of the product.
Design system primitives used rather than forked.
checks_requiring_browser_tooling: Loading, empty, and error states rendered live.
Primary workflow completion end to end.

notes: Checks that could not be performed because tooling was unavailable are listed explicitly, never reported as passing.

failure_conditions: Reporting a browser-dependent check as passed when no browser tooling ran.
Substituting personal visual taste for a standard.
stop_conditions: A primary workflow is broken: BLOCK.
A destructive action has no confirmation: BLOCK.
All required checks completed, with unavailable checks listed.
escalation_conditions: An accessibility defect that blocks a user from completing a primary workflow.
A change that alters an established interaction pattern across the product.
